stages.title: Advanced grammar
stages.hook: Greek has no dative case. How can you say "I give the book to my friend"?
explain: Modern Greek nouns have four cases. The nominative (ο φίλος) is the subject, the genitive (του φίλου) shows possession or "of", the accusative (τον φίλο) marks the object and follows most prepositions, and the vocative (φίλε!) is used when you call someone.

The old dative has disappeared. To mean "to someone" Greek uses σε plus the accusative (Δίνω το βιβλίο στον φίλο μου) or the genitive pronoun (Του δίνω το βιβλίο). The article changes with the case, so learn it with the noun: ο, του, τον.
stages.mnemonic: Ο φίλος, του φίλου, τον φίλο: the article shows the case before the noun does.
sentences: This is the book of my friend.

gq.q: Which case is used to call someone, as in Φίλε!?
gq.why: The vocative is used for direct address.

gq.q: How do you say "to the friend" with σε?
gq.why: Σε plus the accusative of the article becomes στον.

panel.q: How does Greek express "to someone" without a dative?
o: With σε plus the accusative or a genitive pronoun
panel.why: Σε + accusative and the weak genitive pronoun (μου, σου) replace the dative.

panel.q: Why do many Greek names lose -ς when called, like Γιάννης → Γιάννη?
o: The name changes its meaning when it is called
The vocative of -ης names drops the final ς
panel.why: Masculine nouns in -ης drop ς in the vocative.

panel.q: Why must the article be learned with each noun?
o: It is only decoration at the start of words
It is used only in writing
It shows gender, number and case
panel.why: Ο, του, τον show the role of the noun.

teach.model: Modern Greek has four cases: nominative, genitive, accusative and vocative. The old dative is replaced by σε plus accusative or a genitive pronoun. The article changes with the case.

points.ask: How do I say to someone?

trip.prompt: Find the case table for ο φίλος and read the forms aloud.

stages.title: Complex sentence patterns
stages.hook: In "If I had time, I would come" Greek uses a past form in both parts. Why?
explain: A hypothetical (unreal) condition uses a past tense after αν and θα plus a past tense in the result: Αν είχα χρόνο, θα ερχόμουν (If I had time, I would come). For a possible future condition Greek uses αν plus a subjunctive form: Αν βρέξει, θα μείνουμε.

With a different subject Greek uses να plus the verb: Θέλω να έρθεις αύριο. Time clauses use μόλις (as soon as) with a subjunctive: Μόλις φτάσω, θα σε πάρω τηλέφωνο. Use παρόλο που (even though), ώστε (so that) and όχι μόνο... αλλά και (not only... but also) to build longer sentences.
stages.mnemonic: Past in the if-part, past in the θα-part: unreal.
items: If I had time, I would come.
sentences: If I had time, I would come.
I want you to come tomorrow.
As soon as I arrive, I will call you.

gq.q: Which sentence expresses an unreal condition?
gq.why: Past tense in both clauses shows that the condition is not real.

gq.q: How do you say "I want you to come"?
gq.why: Θέλω is followed by να and a verb that agrees with the new subject.

panel.q: What does παρόλο που express?
o: Contrast: even though something is true
panel.why: Παρόλο που is followed by the indicative.

panel.q: Why is μόλις φτάσω without θα?
o: Θα is not a Greek word
Future time clauses use the subjunctive form
panel.why: After μόλις and όταν a future event uses the subjunctive form (φτάσω) without θα.

panel.q: Which word shows purpose?
panel.why: Ώστε means so that.

teach.model: For an unreal condition use a past tense after αν and θα plus a past tense: Αν είχα χρόνο, θα ερχόμουν. For a different subject use να: Θέλω να έρθεις. Use μόλις with the subjunctive for the future.

points.ask: How do I say an unreal condition?
How do I say I want you to come?
How do I say as soon as?

trip.prompt: Find conditional sentences and mark the verb forms.

stages.title: Extended conversations
stages.hook: Greek speakers say "δηλαδή" and "λοιπόν" all the time. What do these little words do?
explain: Extended conversations use connectors. Παρεμπιπτόντως (by the way) adds a related point, στην πραγματικότητα (in reality) corrects an idea, ακριβώς (exactly) confirms, and λοιπόν (well, so) and δηλαδή (that is to say) organise speech.

To disagree gently say Δεν συμφωνώ απόλυτα (I do not completely agree). To ask politely use a plural form: Μπορείτε να με βοηθήσετε; Use Πώς να το πω... when you search for words. Show interest with Σοβαρά; (Really?).
stages.mnemonic: Λοιπόν opens the floor, δηλαδή explains.
sentences: By the way, did you decide?
In reality I do not know.
I do not completely agree with you.

gq.why: Απόλυτα (completely) with δεν makes it gentler.

panel.q: Why is Μπορείτε να με βοηθήσετε; polite?
o: It is a command, but said in a soft voice
panel.why: Plural address is formal.

panel.q: What does δηλαδή do?
o: It asks a price in a shop
panel.why: It means that is to say.

panel.q: Why say Σοβαρά; during a story?
o: To end the talk as soon as possible
panel.why: Back-channel words keep a conversation moving.

teach.model: Use connectors: παρεμπιπτόντως for a side point, στην πραγματικότητα to correct, ακριβώς to confirm, δηλαδή to explain. Disagree gently with Δεν συμφωνώ απόλυτα.

trip.prompt: Read a short dialogue and circle the connecting words.

stages.title: Formal and informal registers
stages.hook: Greek used to have two official forms of the language, one formal and one spoken. Which won?
explain: Formality in Greek is marked by εσύ (informal) and εσείς (formal or plural). Compare Γεια σου with Γεια σας, Δώσε μου (informal) with Δώστε μου (formal) and σε παρακαλώ with σας παρακαλώ. Formal greetings include Χαίρετε and Να είστε καλά (Take care).

For centuries Greek had a formal, archaising form (καθαρεύουσα) and a spoken one (δημοτική). In 1976 the demotic form became the official language of the state, and today formal register is shown mainly by vocabulary and polite forms. A formal letter ends Με εκτίμηση (with esteem).
stages.mnemonic: Εσύ is a smile, εσείς is a polite bow.
sentences: Could you tell me the time?

gq.q: You meet an older neighbour. Which pronoun do you use?
Which closing fits a formal letter?
gq.why: It is the standard formal closing.

panel.q: What happened in 1976 to Greek?
o: Demotic became the official language of the state
Greek was banned from schools and from state offices
panel.why: The language question ended with demotic as the standard.

panel.q: Why does the imperative differ in Δώσε and Δώστε?
o: Δώστε is the past tense form of the same verb here
The -τε ending shows plural or polite address
panel.why: Register is marked in verbs.

panel.q: Why use the plural with a stranger?
o: Strangers always come in groups of two or more people
Plural is a polite way of addressing one person
panel.why: Like French vous, εσείς is formal.

teach.model: Greek marks formality with εσύ and εσείς. Imperatives change: Δώσε and Δώστε. Demotic became the official language in 1976. End a formal letter with Με εκτίμηση.

trip.prompt: Read about katharevousa and demotic and note one difference.

stages.title: Reading articles and literature
stages.hook: Two Greek poets won the Nobel Prize in Literature. Can you name one?
explain: Modern Greek literature includes the poets Konstantinos Kavafis (Cavafy), whose poem Ιθάκη says that the journey matters more than the arrival, Giorgos Seferis (Nobel Prize 1963) and Odysseas Elytis (Nobel Prize 1979). Nikos Kazantzakis wrote the novel Βίος και πολιτεία του Αλέξη Ζορμπά (Zorba the Greek).

To discuss reading, learn genre words: διήγημα (short story), μυθιστόρημα (novel), ποίημα (poem), and analysis words: πλοκή (plot), θέμα (theme). Newspaper articles (άρθρα) in εφημερίδες often use the present tense for recent events.
stages.mnemonic: Ιθάκη: enjoy the road, not only the harbour.
sentences: This is a short story about friendship.
The article talks about the economy.

gq.q: Who wrote the novel about Zorba?
Which poet won the Nobel Prize in 1963?
gq.why: Seferis won the 1963 Nobel Prize in Literature.

panel.q: What is the main idea of Cavafy's poem Ιθάκη?
o: The journey and what you learn matter more than reaching the goal
panel.why: The poem advises that the road brings richness.

panel.q: Why do Greek writers often use ancient myth?
o: Greeks do not read modern stories or modern poetry at all
Myths give shared images that link past and present
panel.why: Poets draw on a long cultural heritage.

panel.q: What is the difference between πλοκή and θέμα?
o: Πλοκή is the sequence of events and θέμα is the main idea
panel.why: Plot tells what happens; theme says what it is about.

teach.model: Cavafy, Seferis and Elytis are major poets, and Kazantzakis wrote Zorba. Analyse a text by plot (πλοκή) and theme (θέμα). Seferis won the Nobel Prize in 1963 and Elytis in 1979.

points.ask: How do I analyse a text?

trip.prompt: Read about Ithaca and summarise its message in one sentence.

stages.title: Essay and correspondence writing
stages.hook: How do you start a formal e-mail in Greek, and how do you finish it?
explain: An essay has εισαγωγή (introduction), κύριο μέρος (main part) and επίλογος (conclusion). Link ideas with αρχικά (at first), έπειτα (then), συνεπώς (therefore) and συμπερασματικά (to conclude).

A formal letter begins Αξιότιμε κύριε or Αξιότιμη κυρία and ends Με εκτίμηση. Use Σας παρακαλώ να... (I ask you to...), Αναφορικά με... (regarding...) and Επισυνάπτω... (I attach...). Keep a clear, polite tone.
stages.mnemonic: Εισαγωγή opens, κύριο μέρος builds, επίλογος closes.

gq.q: How does a formal letter to a woman begin?

panel.q: Which order is typical for an essay?
panel.why: The structure guides the reader.

panel.q: Why use Σας παρακαλώ να instead of a command?
o: It is shorter and more direct
panel.why: Polite requests avoid direct commands.

panel.q: What does Επισυνάπτω tell the reader?
panel.why: It is a formal verb for attaching.

teach.model: An essay has εισαγωγή, κύριο μέρος and επίλογος. Link ideas with αρχικά, έπειτα, συνεπώς and συμπερασματικά. A formal letter begins Αξιότιμε... and ends Με εκτίμηση.

points.ask: How do I start and end a letter?

trip.prompt: Look at a model formal letter and mark the greeting and closing.

stages.title: Translation fundamentals
stages.hook: In Greek "I miss you" is "Μου λείπεις", which literally means "you are missing to me". Why?
explain: Good translation carries meaning, not just words. Μου λείπεις (literally "you are lacking to me") is the natural way to say "I miss you". A literal translation (κατά λέξη μετάφραση) can sound strange or be wrong.

Translators check context (συμφραζόμενα), register and false friends. Greek uses articles more than English, so translating into Greek often means adding ο, η or το. Greek verbs show the person, so the pronoun can disappear in the translation. Idioms need an equivalent expression.
stages.mnemonic: Translate the message: the missing person is "to me".
sentences: Literal translation is not always right.

gq.q: How do you say "I miss you" naturally?
gq.why: The person missed is the subject of λείπω.

gq.q: Why can a literal translation be wrong?
o: Languages express ideas with different structures

panel.q: Why does a translation into Greek often add articles?
o: Greek has no articles, so translators must add them
Articles are optional in all cases
Greek uses the definite article more than English
panel.why: Greek puts the article before names and abstract nouns.

panel.q: What is a good method for translating an idiom?
o: Find an equivalent idiom in the target language
panel.why: Equivalence preserves the effect.

panel.q: Why is context essential?
o: Words never change their meaning in any text
The same word can have several meanings
panel.why: Συμφραζόμενα choose among senses.

teach.model: Translation carries meaning rather than words. Μου λείπεις is the natural way to say I miss you. Check context, register and false friends.

points.ask: How do you say I miss you?

trip.prompt: Read about equivalence and give an example of your own.

stages.title: Regional varieties and cultural context
stages.hook: Greek is the official language of two countries. Which two?
explain: Greek is the official language of Greece and Cyprus. Standard Modern Greek is understood everywhere, but regional speech differs: Cretan, Cypriot and others have special words and sounds. Greek communities live in many countries, for example Australia, the USA and Germany.

Culture shapes daily life. A πανηγύρι is a village festival with music and dance, a καφενείο is a traditional café where people talk, and Πάσχα (Easter) is the biggest celebration. The Orthodox date often differs from the Western date. The greeting is Χριστός Ανέστη! and the reply is Αληθώς Ανέστη!.
stages.mnemonic: Χριστός Ανέστη! and Αληθώς Ανέστη!: a call and its reply.
sentences: In summer we go to the island.
In the café we talk a lot.

gq.q: What do Greeks say at Easter?
Where is Greek an official language?
gq.why: Greek is official in both Greece and Cyprus.

panel.q: Why does regional speech exist in Greek?
o: Language varies over place and history
Greek has no standard form at all, so all differ
panel.why: Dialects develop in different regions.

panel.q: Why is a καφενείο more than a café?
o: It sells only food, never coffee or drinks
It is a social place for conversation
panel.why: It is a community gathering place.

panel.q: Why is Orthodox Easter often on a different date from Western Easter?
o: The two traditions use different calendar calculations
It follows a lunar year only
panel.why: The Orthodox date is computed with the Julian calendar.

teach.model: Greek is official in Greece and Cyprus and has regional varieties such as Cretan and Cypriot. Culture includes πανηγύρι, καφενείο and Πάσχα, with the greeting Χριστός Ανέστη.

points.ask: How do Greeks greet at Easter?

trip.prompt: Read about the customs and note two traditions.

stages.title: Structured debates and presentations
stages.hook: The word "democracy" is Greek. Which two parts make it?
explain: Δημοκρατία comes from δήμος (people) and κράτος (power). Greek political words are often used in debates. A presentation begins with a greeting and the topic: Καλημέρα σας, θα μιλήσω για... A debate uses θέση (thesis), επιχείρημα (argument), παράδειγμα (example) and συμπέρασμα (conclusion).

State your view with Κατά τη γνώμη μου... (In my opinion). Contrast ideas with Από τη μία... από την άλλη... (On the one hand... on the other). Object politely with Επιτρέψτε μου να διαφωνήσω (Allow me to disagree). End with Σας ευχαριστώ για την προσοχή σας.
stages.mnemonic: Θέση, επιχείρημα, παράδειγμα, συμπέρασμα: four steps to persuade.
sentences: In my opinion, this is important.
I would like to give an example.

gq.q: What are the two parts of δημοκρατία?
gq.why: Δήμος means people and κράτος means power.

gq.q: How do you thank the audience?
o: Σας ευχαριστώ για την προσοχή σας
gq.why: It is the standard closing of a talk.

panel.q: Why give an example after an argument?
o: It replaces the argument so that none is needed
It makes the claim concrete and credible
panel.why: Evidence supports the claim.

panel.q: Which is a polite way to disagree?
panel.why: It keeps respect for the other speaker.

panel.q: What does Από τη μία... από την άλλη do?
o: It greets the audience at the beginning
It presents two sides of an issue
panel.why: It balances two views.

teach.model: Start with a greeting and topic. State a θέση, give επιχειρήματα and examples, and end with a συμπέρασμα. Disagree politely with Επιτρέψτε μου να διαφωνήσω and thank the audience.

points.ask: How do I organise a talk?

trip.prompt: Read the origin of the word and note the two Greek parts.
